clue.text: Vermeer somehow encapsulates love, always

indicators.note: 'somehow' suggests the painter's name is put together in some unstated new way
to encapsulate is to enclose something inside a capsule, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: the Dutch painter's name, taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An art critic notes that a Vermeer canvas somehow always captures love.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore is a literary adverb meaning for all time or forever, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Every single train failing to start

indicators.note: a word that fails to start has lost its opening letter

blocks.note: to train someone is to teach them

explanation.surface: A grumbling commuter complains that every single train is failing to set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like the railway noun, but it is the verb meaning to instruct; TEACH without its T leaves EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every single both pick out the members of a group one by one, used before a noun.

clue.text: A guest deduces incorrectly this is not mere conjecture

definitions.note: describes the answer, a noun phrase

indicators.note: done incorrectly means the letters are put in a wrong, jumbled order

blocks.note: the thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A dinner guest reasons badly yet insists the conclusion is no wild guess.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder 'A guest deduces' rearranges into EDUCATED GUESS, and the definition pointedly contrasts it with a mere guess.
explanation.definitionFit: An educated guess rests on knowledge and reasoning, so it is more than a random stab or speculation.

clue.text: Deftly handles lost upset animal

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so these letters wander out of their order

blocks.note: both words taken as written for their letters

explanation.surface: A vet deftly handles a lost and frightened creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' seems to be the anagram signal, but it belongs to the fodder; 'lost' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To manipulate is to work or control something skilfully with the hands, as a craftsman or physiotherapist does.

clue.text: Right editor on very good paper

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
ED is the usual short form of editor
top means excellent or first-rate

explanation.surface: A proud journalist boasts that the right editor sits on a very good newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A red-top is a British tabloid newspaper, named after the red mastheads of titles like The Sun and the Mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a red-top is a downmarket tabloid newspaper, so it is a kind of paper.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying unknown leader once

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
in algebra unknowns are written x, y and z

explanation.surface: A car carries some mysterious figure who used to be in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The czar, or tsar, was the emperor of Russia until 1917, a ruler from the past.

clue.text: Way of changing sides laid out in black and white?

definitions.text: Way of changing sides laid out in black and white?

blocks.clueFragment: Way of changing sides laid out in black and white?
blocks.note: surface reading: a plan for defecting to the other team, set out plainly in writing

blocks.clueFragment: Way of changing sides laid out in black and white?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a striped road marking that lets pedestrians cross from one side of the street to the other

explanation.walkthrough: 'In black and white' usually means written down; here it is literal, the stripes of a British pedestrian crossing. 'Changing sides' is crossing the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A zebra crossing is a British pedestrian crossing painted with black and white stripes across the road.

clue.text: Underwent an experience again, full of energy and happy

indicators.note: something full of a substance holds it inside, so one piece is filled with another

blocks.note: to relive is to go through an experience a second time
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone revisits a thrilling memory, full of energy and delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Relieved means glad and freed from worry, so it fits as a near synonym for pleased or content.

clue.text: Heave big container alongside church

indicators.note: alongside means placed next to, so the two pieces simply sit side by side

blocks.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church
an urn is a large vessel, such as a tea urn

explanation.surface: Volunteers heave a huge tea urn next to the church hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The church piece comes first even though it is mentioned last.
explanation.definitionFit: To churn is to move or heave about violently, as the sea or a stomach does.

clue.text: Amount of sound indicated by central part of soundboard?

blocks.clueFragment: indicated by central part of soundboard?
blocks.note: surface reading: a level shown on the middle of a mixing desk

blocks.clueFragment: indicated by central part of soundboard?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the two middle letters of soundboard spell the unit's abbreviation, dB

explanation.surface: A sound engineer reads the volume off the middle of the mixing desk.
explanation.walkthrough: Soundboard has ten letters; the fifth and sixth are D and B, and dB is the symbol for this unit of loudness.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is the unit measuring loudness, so it expresses a quantity of sound.

clue.text: My family member provides a connection

blocks.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'
a relation is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone explains how a relative turns out to link two people together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is an exclamation, matched by the British 'Cor!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A correlation is a mutual relationship or link between two things, especially in statistics.

clue.text: Fitting take

blocks.note: first meaning: suitable, proper for the occasion (adjective)
second meaning: to seize something for oneself (verb), with stress on the last syllable

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: the adjective ends '-ət', the verb ends '-ate'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as an adjective for suitable and as a verb for seizing or commandeering possession.

clue.text: Recovers from Las Vegas revelling

indicators.note: revelling suggests wild partying, so the letters are thrown about in disorder

blocks.note: the city's name taken as written

explanation.surface: A partygoer recovers after a wild weekend in Las Vegas.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage is to rescue or retrieve something from loss or wreckage, so it means to recover.

clue.text: Ancient ewer principally covered with a precious metal

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or first of all, so only the opening letter is wanted
something covered with a layer is wrapped by it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: taken as written
gold is a precious metal
the first letter of ewer

explanation.surface: A museum piece: an ancient jug plated with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: A ewer is a large water jug.
explanation.definitionFit: Age-old means having existed for a very long time, so it is a synonym for very old.

clue.text: Branch seen in river? Good heavens!

indicators.note: something seen in a place sits inside it, so one piece lies within another

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
an arm is a branch or offshoot, as of a river or an organisation

explanation.surface: Someone spots a fallen tree branch floating in the river and exclaims.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear me is a mild exclamation of surprise or dismay, used just as Good heavens is.

clue.text: Marriage partner will reportedly show anger

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: a bride is a marriage partner, and 'bride will' contracts to bride'll

explanation.surface: A spouse is said to be about to lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' is not a separate word to drop; it fuses with the partner into a contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to show resentment or anger, like a horse jerking its head back against the reins.

clue.text: A tavern is struggling to accommodate eg, plant eaters

indicators.note: something struggling flails about, so the letters lose their order
to accommodate a guest is to house them inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: taken as written for the letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A failing pub tries to cater for customers who avoid meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetarians eat no meat, living on foods from plants, so they are herbivores in a loose sense.

clue.text: Celeb ultimately craves that extra honour

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the final letter of each following word is used

blocks.note: the last letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A celebrity hungers for one more award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' seems to qualify 'Celeb', but it applies to each of the four words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeb is a celebrity, and a famous performer is commonly called a star.

clue.text: Given lubrication, outer parts of gear moved smoothly

indicators.note: the outer parts of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of gear
to ease is to move something gently and smoothly

explanation.surface: Once oiled, the outside of the gear turned without a hitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Greased means smeared with oil or fat to reduce friction, the same as lubricated.

clue.text: Silly passport, possibly with nothing in it

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a passport is one example of identification
taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly carries a passport with no pages in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' reads as an adjective, but here it is the noun, as when someone is called 'you silly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly, used as a noun, is a foolish person, and an idiot is a stupid person.

clue.text: Mediocre serving of miso soup

indicators.note: a serving is a portion, so only part of the following words is taken

blocks.note: the letters running across the end of miso and the start of soup

explanation.surface: A diner rates a bowl of miso soup as nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means neither good nor bad, merely middling or average.

clue.text: They’re extremely keen to welcome new youngster

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word before it, its first and last letters
to welcome a visitor is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the first and last letters of They're, ignoring the apostrophe
eager means keen
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Young people are said to be ever so keen to greet a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like it intensifies 'keen', but it selects the ends of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a person aged thirteen to nineteen, so a young person or adolescent.
